# Stint reference

Every command, setting, file, environment variable, exit code and JSON key of Stint, and the order
in which `stint next` decides. For tasks, see the [how-to guides](how-to.md); for what it cannot do,
see the [limitations](limitations.md).

## Commands

`stint` runs in the session's Bash tool, where Stint puts it on the `PATH`; the skills run it for
you. Every command takes `--json` to print its payload instead of one text line. If `stint` is not
found, run `python "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/stint.py"` with the same arguments. The table is
read from the plugin's own command parser.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `stint add` | Queue an item. |
| `stint list` | List the items. |
| `stint report` | Count the items finished since the run started, and those running or pending. |
| `stint start` | Start a pending item (takes a PaceLine hold when PaceLine is found). |
| `stint done` | Finish an item (releases its hold). |
| `stint fail` | Count a failed attempt; the third defers the item and its dependents. |
| `stint defer` | Defer an item and every item that depends on it. |
| `stint retry` | Put an item back to pending. |
| `stint remove` | Remove an item. |
| `stint clear-done` | Remove the done items. |
| `stint config` | Show the settings, or change them. |
| `stint next` | Answer start, wait or stop for the next item (exit 0, 10 or 11). |

### Queue commands

- `add --title TEXT --repo NAME --estimate PCT [--independent] [--depends ID,ID]` queues an item
  with the next id `Q<n>`. `--independent` lets it run beside other independent items. Every
  dependency must already exist. With PaceLine, `add` also prints the hint for tonight's share of 0
  (see [Tonight's share](how-to.md#plan-tonights-share)).
- `list` lists the items with their status, estimate, dependencies and, for a deferred item, its
  reason. `report` counts the items finished since the current run started (all items when there is
  no run) and the running and pending ones, with the sums of the done items' estimates and actual
  costs.
- `start ID [--pid N]` turns a pending item into a running one and records when it started and the
  week's usage then. With PaceLine it also takes a `queue` hold with the key `stint-<id>`, which
  PaceLine keeps for 240 minutes. An item that is not pending is refused.
- `done ID [--actual PCT]` marks the item done and releases its hold; a hold that cannot be released
  stays on the item. The actual cost defaults to the week's usage now minus the usage at start, not
  below 0; it stays unknown when either is unknown.
- `fail ID [--reason TEXT]` counts one failed attempt. At the third, the item is deferred, with the
  reason `gates failed after 3 fix attempts` unless `--reason` gives one.
- `defer ID [--reason TEXT]` defers the item and, transitively, every pending or running item that
  depends on it, and releases their holds. An item that is not pending or running is refused:
  `stint: <id> is <status>, not pending or running`. The default reason is `needs owner permission`;
  the dependents get `depends on deferred <id>`.
- `retry ID` puts an item back to pending and resets its failure count. `remove ID` deletes an item;
  it is refused while a pending or running item depends on it. `clear-done` deletes the done items.

An item is `pending`, `running`, `done` or `deferred`. Ids match case-insensitively.

### stint next

`next [--start-run]` answers whether the next item may start. It exits `0` for start, `10` for wait
and `11` for stop, and prints one line:

- `next: START <id> | budget <b>% | agents <=<n>`, with the reasons appended after ` | ` when there
  are any;
- `next: WAIT until <time> | <reasons>`, or `next: WAIT | <reasons>` when no time is known;
- `next: STOP | <reasons>`. Reasons are joined by `; `.

`--start-run` opens a run unless one is open: a run is open until it has `ended_at`, while its end
is null or later than now and, with PaceLine, the account is the same. `next` closes the open run at
the first stop it answers: the run gets `ended_at`, counts as no run from then on, and the next
`--start-run` opens a new one. Then that run is kept and the answer has `reused` true. A new run
archives the old one (the last 14 are kept) and stores the start, the end, the account, the source,
the budget at that moment and the week's usage. With PaceLine the end is `night.end` of `paceline
status --json`, the end of tonight's off-hours part; without PaceLine it is null.

### stint config

`config [--week-stop PCT] [--five-hour-stop PCT] [--agents N]` shows the three settings, each with
its default, whether PaceLine was found and which program, and the age of the usage reading. With an
option it first writes the value. A value out of range or not a whole number is an error and nothing
is written.

## Settings

Stint has three settings, which it applies when PaceLine does not decide. The table is read from the
plugin's own constants. They live in `<state>/settings.json`, and each field falls back to its
default on its own when the file lacks it or holds an invalid value.

| Key | Option of stint config | Default | Range |
|---|---|---|---|
| `week_stop_pct` | `--week-stop` | `85` | 50–100 |
| `five_hour_stop_pct` | `--five-hour-stop` | `95` | 50–100 |
| `agents` | `--agents` | `3` | 1–6 |

- `week_stop_pct`: at or above this share of the week, the run stops.
- `five_hour_stop_pct`: at or above this share of the five-hour window, the run waits until it
  resets.
- `agents`: the number of parallel agents `stint next` allows when it starts an item without
  PaceLine.

With PaceLine, the budget and the agents come from PaceLine's advice, and the settings apply only
when its advice is unavailable.

## Skills

Two skills run the commands in a session:

- `/stint:queue` adds, lists and changes items and asks you before running the command of the
  tonight's-share hint.
- `/stint:run` works the queue: it starts the run, loops over `stint next`, and fills the morning
  report from `templates/morning-report.md`. It chooses the model of each item itself; with PaceLine
  it reads the model-scoped weekly buckets from `paceline status --json`, without it no scoped
  figures exist.

## How next decides with PaceLine

Stint runs `paceline advice --json`. The advice is valid when the output is a JSON object with
`advice_version` 1, an `action` of start, wait or stop and a list of reasons, whatever the exit
code. Anything else (no output, a timeout, another version) makes the advice invalid: Stint's own
order applies, `source` is `stint`, and the reasons end with `PaceLine's advice unavailable (<why>):
Stint's own stops apply`. With a valid advice, the first match wins:

1. No run, or a run that has `ended_at`: stop, `no run: start one with stint next --start-run`.
2. The run's account and the advice's are both known and differ: stop, `account changed during the
   run`.
3. The run's end is reached: stop, `night ended`.
4. An advice reason has the effect `stop` and the code `memory`, `weekly` or `weekly_scoped`: stop,
   with the advice's reason texts.
5. The run's account is known and the advice's is null: wait, `account unknown`.
6. The queue is empty: stop, `queue empty`. Only deferred items are left: stop, `all remaining items
   need owner permission`.
7. The advice says stop: stop, with the advice's reason texts.
8. The advice says wait: when its `wait_until` is null or before the run's end (or the end is null),
   wait until the advice's `wait_until`, with its texts; otherwise stop, with its texts and `nothing
   can start before the night ends`.
9. No pending item fits the budget: stop, `budget exhausted: no item fits <budget>%`. Items are
   running or dependencies unfinished: wait, `waiting for running items or dependencies`.
10. Otherwise start the item. The budget is the advice's `budget_pct`, the agents are its `agents`,
    and the reasons are the texts of its `limit` reasons.

## How next decides without PaceLine

Without PaceLine, or with an invalid advice, the first match wins. Percentages in the texts are
whole numbers.

1. No run, or a run that has `ended_at`: stop, `no run: start one with stint next --start-run`.
2. The run's end is reached: stop, `night ended`.
3. No reading, or one without the week bucket (`seven_day`): wait, `no usage reading yet: Stint
   reads the limits Claude Code hands to a session`. A reading older than 30 minutes: wait, `usage
   data stale (<n> min)`.
4. The week is at or above `week_stop_pct`: stop, `week <w>% >= <s>% stop`.
5. The queue is empty or only deferred items are left: stop, as in step 6 with PaceLine.
6. The five-hour window is at or above `five_hour_stop_pct`: wait until its reset, `5h window
   <u>% >= <s>% stop, resets <time>` (`resets later` when no reset time is known).
7. The item rules with the budget `week_stop_pct` minus the week's usage, not below 0: as in step 9
   with PaceLine.
8. Otherwise start the item, with `agents` agents and no reasons.

A bucket whose reset time has passed reads as 0%. A reading is stale when it is more than 30 minutes
old.

## Item rules

Both orders choose the item the same way. The next item is the first pending one whose dependencies
are done and whose estimate fits the budget. An item that is not independent never runs beside
another item, and no item runs beside it. When there is no such item, the rule gives one of four
results:

- `empty`: no items are left to run.
- `blocked`: only deferred dependencies or deferred items are left.
- `waiting`: items are running or dependencies are unfinished.
- `budget`: pending items remain but none fits the budget.

## JSON keys

With `--json`, a command prints its payload. The table gives the text line of each command and the
keys of its payload.

| Command | Text line | JSON keys |
|---|---|---|
| `add` | `queue Q<n> added (<estimate>%), pending total <sum>%`, then the hint line when there is one | `item`, `pending_total_pct`, `tonight_off_share_pct`, `tonight_off_hint` |
| `list` | one line per item, or `queue empty` | `items` |
| `report` | `done <n> (est <sum>% act <sum>%), deferred <n>, running <n>, pending <n>` | `run`, `done`, `deferred`, `running`, `pending`, `estimate_sum_pct`, `actual_sum_pct` |
| `start` | `<id> started`, with `, hold <hold id>` when a PaceLine hold was taken | `item` |
| `done` | `<id> done, estimate <e>% actual <a>%` | `item` |
| `fail` | `<id> failed attempt <a>/3, keep fixing`, or at the third `deferred <ids>: <reason>` | `item`, `deferred` |
| `defer` | `deferred <ids>: <reason>` | `deferred` |
| `retry` | `<id> back to pending` | `item` |
| `remove` | `<id> removed` | `removed` |
| `clear-done` | `cleared <n> done item(s)` | an empty object |
| `config` | the settings, PaceLine and the reading | `settings`, `defaults`, `paceline`, `reading_age_min` |
| `next` | see [stint next](#stint-next) | see the lists below |

The JSON of `next` has these keys:

- `action` (`start`, `wait` or `stop`), `may_start_next_item` and `max_parallel_agents` (0 unless
  start).
- `budget_for_next_item_pct`: the advice's `budget_pct` with PaceLine, Stint's own budget otherwise,
  0 when there is no run.
- `next_item`: the item's `id`, `title`, `repo`, `estimate_pct`, `independent`, `depends_on`,
  `status`, `reason`, `attempts` and `actual_pct`; null unless start.
- `wait_until` (only on wait, else null) and `reasons` (strings).
- `run`: `started_at`, `ended_at` (null while the run is open), `end`, `source`, `allowance_pct`
  (the budget when the run started, informational), `spent_pct` (the week's usage now minus the
  usage at start, not below 0, null when unknown) and `reused`; null when there is no run.
- `source`: `paceline` or `stint`, whose limits decided. `advice`: PaceLine's advice, or null.
- `limits`, when Stint's own stops decide: `week_pct`, `five_hour_pct`, `five_hour_resets_at`,
  `age_min`, `week_stop_pct` and `five_hour_stop_pct`, null where unknown; null with PaceLine.

## Files and folders

`<state>` is Stint's state directory: `$STINT_STATE_DIR` when set, else `<config>/state/stint`.
`<config>` is `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, else `~/.claude`. `<legacy>` is PaceLine's:
`$PACELINE_STATE_DIR`, else `<config>/state/paceline`.

| Path | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `<state>/queue.json` | The queue: `run`, `past_runs`, `next_id` and `items`. Written whole, as UTF-8 with LF, by an atomic replace, under `queue.lock`. An unreadable file or one that is not a JSON object is an error that names the file, and so is an `items` entry that is not an object; the file is never overwritten. |
| `<state>/queue.lock` | The lock of the queue, created exclusively; it holds a token of its own, and only the command with that token deletes it. A writer waits up to 10 seconds; a lock older than 300 seconds is taken over. |
| `<state>/settings.json` | The settings `week_stop_pct`, `five_hour_stop_pct` and `agents`. Written by `stint config`. |
| `<state>/limits.json` | The last usage reading: `observed_at`, `session_id` and the buckets `five_hour` and `seven_day`, each with `used_percentage` and `resets_at`. Written by the module of the plugin, when the figures changed or a minute passed since the last write. |
| `<legacy>/night-queue.json` | PaceLine's queue. Read only while `<state>/queue.json` does not exist; never written, moved or deleted. A run in it may carry `night_end`, which Stint reads as the run's end. A file that cannot be read or is not a JSON object gives one line on stderr, `stint: PaceLine's queue <path> cannot be read (<why>); starting from an empty queue`, and an empty queue. |
| `<state>/night-power-state.json` | The power settings that `night-power.ps1 -Enable` saved, restored by `-Disable`. |
| `<legacy>/night-power-state.json` | The file PaceLine's copy of the script wrote. `-Disable` reads it only when Stint's file is absent. |

PaceLine's leftover pool file is not read.

## Environment variables

| Variable | What it does |
|---|---|
| `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` | Claude Code's configuration directory. Stint's state directory and PaceLine's are under it. Unset or empty: `~/.claude`. |
| `HOME` | Where the module finds the home directory to compute `<config>` when `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` and `USERPROFILE` are not set. |
| `PACELINE_STATE_DIR` | PaceLine's state directory, which Stint reads the legacy queue from. Unset or empty: `<config>/state/paceline`. |
| `STINT_NOW` | The current instant as an ISO 8601 time, for tests. Unset: the clock. A value that is not a time is an error. |
| `STINT_PACELINE` | `off`: Stint ignores PaceLine. A path: the program to call (a path ending in `.py` runs with the current Python; one ending in `.cmd` or `.bat` is never run: Stint runs the `scripts/paceline.py` beside the launcher's folder with the current Python, and counts PaceLine as not found when that file is missing). Unset: `paceline` on the `PATH`. |
| `STINT_STATE_DIR` | Stint's state directory. Unset or empty: `<config>/state/stint`. |
| `USERPROFILE` | Where the module finds the home directory to compute `<config>` when `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is not set; when it is unset or empty, `HOME` is the fallback. |

The module reads the variables from the environment Claude Code starts in; the scripts read them
from the environment of the command. Stint's calls into PaceLine run in the caller's environment.
`night-power.ps1` reads `STINT_STATE_DIR`, `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` and `PACELINE_STATE_DIR` too. The
table is checked against the variables Stint's code reads.

## Exit codes

- `0`: success; for `next`, start. A failed PaceLine hold call keeps `0` and prints `stint: PaceLine
  hold not taken: <why>` or `stint: PaceLine hold not released: <why>` on stderr.
- `10`: `next` says wait.
- `11`: `next` says stop.
- `2`: an invalid command line or input, with the message on stderr as `stint: ...`, for example
  `stint: unknown dependencies: Q9`, `stint: no item Q9`, `stint: Q1 is done, not pending`, `stint:
  Q1 has dependents Q2; defer or remove them first`, `stint: week_stop_pct must be 50-100`, or a
  queue file that cannot be read or locked.

## Module

Stint has no command hooks. Its `hooks/hooks.json` loads one module, `hooks/register.tsx`, which
handles one event:

- `session.measure`: writes the limits Claude Code hands to plugins (the figures of the status line)
  to `<state>/limits.json`, when the figures changed or a minute passed since the last write. A
  failed write is swallowed and never changes the step. It writes whether or not PaceLine is
  installed.

## Requirements

- Claude Code 2.1.287 or later.
- Python 3.9 or later on `PATH` as `python3` or `python`. Stint uses the standard library only.
- Optional: PaceLine, for the advice. See [Limitations](limitations.md#alongside-paceline).
